''The Acolyte'' is a mystery thriller that will take us into a galaxy of shadowy secrets and emerging Dark Side powers in the final days of the High Republic era.|President Kathleen Kennedy announces the series during Disney Investor Day 2020|{{DisneyCompany|url=disney-investor-day-2020|text=Disney Investor Day 2020}}}} '''''Star Wars: The Acolyte''''' is a ''[[Star Wars]]'' television series developed by [[Leslye Headland]] for [[Disney+]]. Headland wrote, executive produced, and served as the series' showrunner. It takes place a century before the events of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], and focuses on the emergence of [[Dark side of the Force|dark side powers]] in the final [[Standard day|days]] of the [[High Republic Era]]. ''The Acolyte'' premiered on [[June 4]], [[2024]], concluded its first season on [[July 16]], 2024, and was reported as canceled on [[August 19]], 2024, which was later confirmed by Disney executives. In spite of that ending, details have emerged that the series was intended to run for several seasons. ==Official description== ''The Acolyte is a mystery-thriller that will take viewers into a galaxy of shadowy secrets and emerging dark-side powers in the final days of the High Republic era. A former Padawan reunites with her Jedi Master to investigate a series of crimes, but the forces they confront are more sinister than they ever anticipated.'' ==Development== ===Conception and announcements=== {{Quote|I think you see more morally ambiguous characters than you've seen in other Star Wars content. And I think I can say this pretty confidently: I don't think you're going to see action in other shows the way that you see it used and utilized in our show. I just thought it was very interesting to do a show about the bad guys and to set that during that period made the most sense, so I think that's what sets it apart. It's kind of almost flipped. We have more Jedi than you've seen in any other of the Star Wars content. I can say this pretty confidently, I don't think you're going to see action in other shows the way that you see it utilized in our show.|Leslye Headland|{{WebCite|url=https://www.cultureslate.com/news/the-acolyte-showrunner-promising-more-action-more-jedi-and-more-moral-ambiguity-than-ever-before|text='The Acolyte' Showrunner Promising More Action, More Jedi, And More Moral Ambiguity Than Ever Before|date=2023-07-21|work=[https://www.cultureslate.com ''CultureSlate'']|archivedate=20230801033433}}}} [[File:The_Acolyte_pitch_cover.png|thumb|right|300px|The cover to the original pitch deck Leslye Headland used when pitching the series to Lucasfilm in 2019, with imagery created by artist Inga Headland]] [[Leslye Headland]], having served as co-creator for the [[2019]] [[Wikipedia:Russian Doll (TV series)|''Russian Doll'']] television series, in her words "essentially cold-called [[Lucasfilm]]"{{WebCite|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/05/29/arts/television/leslye-headland-the-acolyte.html|text=Leslye Headland Hopes the Force Is With 'The Acolyte'|author=Brooks Barnes|date=2024-05-29|work=[[Wikipedia:The New York Times|''The New York Times'']]|archiveurl=https://archive.is/0AqWX}} in 2019{{WebCite|url=https://www.ingaheadland.com/work/the-acolyte-pitch|text=The Acolyte Pitch Deck|author=[[Inga Headland]]|work=[https://www.ingaheadland.com Inga Headland]|archivedate=20250406220745}} and pitched what would become ''The Acolyte'' as a cross between [[The Walt Disney Company|Disney's]] [[2013]] film [[Wikipedia:Frozen (2013 film)|''Frozen'']] and [[Wikipedia:Quentin Tarantino|Quentin Tarantino's]] [[2003]] film [[Wikipedia:Kill Bill: Volume 1|''Kill Bill'']]. For the initial pitch to Lucasfilm, Headland worked with her sister [[Inga Headland]] to design a [[Wikipedia:Presentation slide|pitch deck]] of imagery paired with story details for the presentation, the cover of which featured a woman in dark clothing cloaked in fog, with the title "Acolyte" displayed above. The series' main characters of [[Verosha Aniseya|Verosha "Osha" Aniseya]] and [[Mae-ho Aniseya|Mae-ho "Mae" Aniseya]] were inspired by Headland's relationship with her youngest sister, and Lucasfilm's President [[Kathleen Kennedy]] told Headland to fashion her ''[[Star Wars]]'' story akin to her "incredibly emotional" play [[Wikipedia:Cult of Love|''Cult of Love'']] about siblinghood. Kennedy responded to Headland's early scripts in 2019: "You've written a great ''Star Wars'' show. Now go write a Leslye Headland show.''" On [[April 22]], [[2020]], [[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']] reported that Leslye Headland was writing and serving as showrunner for a ''Star Wars'' series that would be released on the [[Disney+]] streaming platform. The report noted that the series will be female-centric and take place in a new part of the ''Star Wars'' timeline.{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2020/tv/news/star-wars-series-leslye-headland-disney-plus-1234587493|text='Star Wars' Series From 'Russian Doll' Co-Creator Leslye Headland in the Works at Disney Plus (EXCLUSIVE)|author=Joe Otterson|date=2020-04-22|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20200504201935}} An official announcement on [[May 4]], 2020 on [[StarWars.com]] added that Headland will be an executive producer on the project. The series's title, logo, and general premise were revealed at a Disney investors' meeting on [[December 10]], 2020.{{SW|url=news/future-lucasfilm-projects-revealed|text=Future Lucasfilm Projects Revealed}} Lucasfilm's website also listed vice president of film development [[Rayne Roberts]] as co-developing the series with Headland.{{Lucasfilm|url=leadership/rayne-roberts|text=Rayne Roberts}} [[File:Acolyte-BTS.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Amandla Stenberg, Lee Jung-jae, and director Leslye Headland]] Following a conversation between director [[Kogonada]] and actress [[Jodie Turner-Smith]] at the premiere of their film [[Wikipedia:After Yang|''After Yang'']] at the [[Wikipedia:Cannes Film Festival|Cannes Film Festival]] in July [[2021]], Kogonada offered Turner-Smith the role of Mother [[Aniseya]].{{WebCite|url=https://www.glamourmagazine.co.uk/article/jodie-turner-smith-interview-2024-glamour-women-of-the-year-awards|text=Jodie Turner-Smith: 'We don't get to fail upward like a lot of white men'|author=Iana Murray|date=2024-10-02|work=[[Wikipedia:Glamour (magazine)|''Glamour'']]|archivedate=20241003115534}} According to a [[March 7]], [[2023]], court filing obtained by [[Wikipedia:Deadline Hollywood|''Deadline'']],{{WebCite|url=https://deadline.com/2023/03/star-wars-series-the-acolyte-lawsuit-lucasfilm-karyn-mccarthy-1235282595|text=Lucasfilm Sued For Suddenly Firing 'The Acolyte' EP Karyn McCarthy|author=Dominic Patten|date=2023-03-08|work=[[Wikipedia:Deadline Hollywood|''Deadline'']]|archivedate=20230308184431}} with the filing alleging that Executive Producer Karyn McCarthy had been fired from ''The Acolyte'' after only two weeks of work on the project, Lucasfilm's business plans and ''The Acolyte''{{'s}} story arc as of [[April 7]], [[2022]], called for several seasons. The filing further claims that a heavily guarded Series Overview for those multiple seasons existed by that time, as did a Season One Bible.{{WebCite|url=https://deadline.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/03/lucasfilm-producer.pdf|text=SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF CALIFORINA FOR THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES|format=PDF|archivedate=20240613154819}} On [[July 22]], 2022, [[Amandla Stenberg]] announced alongside the ''Star Wars'' account on [[Wikipedia:Instagram|Instagram]] that she has been cast in the series. On [[November 7]], 2022, StarWars.com announced that the series began production in the [[Wikipedia:United Kingdom|United Kingdom]] and revealed several additional cast members. In July 2023, Headland gave a statement on the show's tone and characters, promising a morally grey look into the ''Star Wars'' universe and unique action. ===Inspiration and filming=== {{Quote|She's like an orchestra director. She has an eye on everything very calmly from above, navigating with such kindness and grace. And because she's such a passionate, creative person, she has such love for every single craft on set. She was always so excited and she had so much respect for everyone. And that's really rare.''"
"''I love somebody who's unafraid to live in who they are and their energy unapologetically. Most people in the world are attracted to that kind of freedom.|Dafne Keen and Charlie Barnett, on Leslye Headland's direction|{{SW|url=news/the-acolyte-charlie-barnett-dafne-keen-interview|text=For the Love of The Acolyte's Jecki Lon and Yord Fandar}}}} ====Literary and ''Star Wars'' influences==== Leslye Headland drew from storytelling in both the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, such as its 1990s roleplaying games as part of what was then known as the "Expanded Universe" beyond the stories of ''[[Star Wars]]'' creator [[George Lucas]], and the ongoing ''[[Star Wars: The High Republic]]'' multimedia project that was launched by Lucasfilm Publishing in 2021. The concept of an acolyte, after which the series is titled, was taken from the Legends continuity; a [[Sith acolyte|Sith Acolyte]] refers to an individual being trained for the position of a [[Sith]]'s formal [[Sith apprentice|apprentice]]. Headland included [[Vernestra Rwoh]], who was introduced as a [[Jedi]] [[Padawan]] learner in [[Justina Ireland]]'s 2021 novel [[The High Republic: A Test of Courage|''A Test of Courage'']], set during the golden age of the [[Galactic Republic]]'s [[democracy]] and the [[Jedi Order]] in the [[High Republic Era]] in [[232 BBY]]. ''The Acolyte'' is set a hundred years afterward and stars Rwoh as a [[Jedi Master]]. The series is also set a hundred years before [[George Lucas]]' [[prequel trilogy]].{{WebCite|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2022/05/the-acolyte-star-wars-series|text=''The Acolyte'': How ''Star Wars'' Is About to Venture Back in Time|author=Anthony Breznican|date=2022-05-22|work=[[Wikipedia:Vanity Fair (magazine)|''Vanity Fair'']]|archivedate=20220524163919}} Headland thought about [[Jedi Master]]s [[Mace Windu]] and [[Yoda]]'s remarks about the relative dormancy of the [[dark side of the Force]] in the [[1999]] prequel film, [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], asking who would have been practicing the dark side in the century leading up to the [[Sith]]'s return and the rise of the [[Galactic Empire]], as shown in [[2002]]'s [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']] and [[2005]]'s [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']]. Headland also compares the time of the High Republic in which ''The Acolyte'' is set to the isolationist tendencies of the [[Wikipedia:United States|United States]] post-[[Wikipedia:World War I|World War I]], particularly in terms of the decay of the High Republic to the time of the [[prequel trilogy]], when [[Darth Sidious]] infiltrated the [[Galactic Senate]]. In terms of spirituality in ''Star Wars'', Headland felt that the concept of the Force as explained by Yoda in ''The Empire Strikes Back'' strongly resonated with her, as compared to "even" the [[Wikipedia:English people|English]] author [[Wikipedia:J. R. R. Tolkien|J.R.R. Tolkien]], whose [[Wikipedia:The Lord of the Rings|''The Lord of the Rings'']] fantasy was published in the [[1950s]], or her own [[Wikipedia:Catholic Church|Catholic]] upbringing. The fantasy aspect of [[the galaxy]] far, far away also prompted her to compare it to the realm of [[Wikipedia:The Chronicles of Narnia|Narnia]] created by [[Wikipedia:C. S. Lewis|C. S. Lewis]], a contemporary of Tolkien's. Headland had a tattoo printed on her right hand after Lucasfilm hired her for ''The Acolyte'', serving as a reminder of ''Star Wars'' to herself while making the series—the tattoo shows [[Ralph McQuarrie]]'s concept illustration of [[Princess]] [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]] for Lucas' [[original trilogy]], released between [[1977]] and [[1983]].{{SW|url=news/leslye-headland-interview|text="Whatever You Think ''The Acolyte'' Is, It's Not": ''Star Wars'' Series Creator Leslye Headland Revels in the First Teaser Trailer}} ====Cinematic influences==== =====Hong Kong Chinese martial arts and Japanese samurai cinema===== Headland also drew inspiration from her favorite martial arts films. The [[Wikipedia:Hong Kong action cinema|Hong Kong]] [[Wikipedia:Shaw Brothers Studio|Shaw Brothers Studio]] film [[Wikipedia:Come Drink with Me|''Come Drink with Me'']]—directed by [[Wikipedia:King Hu|King Hu]], set in the [[Wikipedia:Ming dynasty|Ming era]] (1368—1644), and released in [[1960s|1966]] under the [[Wikipedia:Traditional Chinese characters|Chinese]] title 大醉俠—features a sequence at an inn that forms the basis of the [[Lomi Usqi Noodle Shop]] at the opening of ''The Acolyte''{{'s}} first episode, "[[Lost / Found]]."{{SW|url=lost-found-trivia-gallery-the-acolyte|text="Lost / Found" Trivia Gallery | The Acolyte}} {{C|Slide 1}} The fight sequence there between Jedi Master [[Indara]] and the assassin [[Mae-ho Aniseya|Mae]] also pays homage to the martial arts choreography of [[Wikipedia:Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon|''Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon'']], a [[2000]] [[Wikipedia:Ang Lee|Ang Lee]] film titled in Chinese as 臥虎藏龍.{{SW|url=lost-found-trivia-gallery-the-acolyte|text="Lost / Found" Trivia Gallery | The Acolyte}} {{C|Slide 8}} Aside from [[Wikipedia:Wuxia#Film_and_television|Chinese martial arts films]], known as "mouhap" in [[Wikipedia:Cantonese|Cantonese]] and "wuxia" in [[Wikipedia:Mandarin Chinese|Mandarin]], Headland was also inspired by the [[Wikipedia:Samurai cinema|Japanese samurai]] film [[Wikipedia:Yojimbo|''Yojimbo'']], directed by [[Wikipedia:Akira Kurosawa|Akira Kurosawa]] and released under the [[Wikipedia:Japanese language|Japanese]] title 用心棒 in 1961. She explained that ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'' producer [[Jon Favreau]] had mentioned that George Lucas had been influenced by Kurosawa's filmmaking and [[Wikipedia:Western film|Western films]], and Headland herself based her cinematic influences more strongly on martial arts films such as Shaw Brothers and King Hu productions—naming ''Come Drink with Me'' alongside King Hu's 1971 film [[Wikipedia:A Touch of Zen|''A Touch of Zen'']], in Chinese titled 俠女—that are "less global and galactic," with deeply personal missions in which the warriors felt "wronged" and had to "make it right." As a mystery thriller, ''The Acolyte'' was influenced by Kurosawa's film [[Wikipedia:Rashomon|''Rashomon'']], released in [[1950s|1950]] under the Japanese title 羅生門, for its use of differing interpretations of the same events. Cinematographer [[Chris Teague]] additionally cited the 1973 [[Wikipedia:Toshiya Fujita (director)|Toshiya Fujita]] film [[Wikipedia:Lady Snowblood (film)|''Lady Snowblood'']], a period drama titled 修羅雪姫 in Japanese, as an inspiration for ''The Acolyte''{{'s}} camerawork.{{WebCite|url=https://arstechnica.com/culture/2024/06/star-wars-behind-the-scenes-creating-the-unique-aesthetic-of-the-acolyte|text=Star Wars behind the scenes: Creating the unique aesthetic of The Acolyte|author=Jennifer Ouellette|date=2024-06-26|work=[[Wikipedia:Ars Technica|''Ars Technica'']]|archiveurl=https://archive.is/CuDKv}} =====Character inspirations===== Headland compared the story of Mae to ''Frozen'' and ''Kill Bill'', and the character was also inspired by the story of [[Ahsoka Tano]] in the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series' 2013 episode "[[The Wrong Jedi]]" and the dynamic between [[Qi'ra]] and [[Maul]] at the end of the 2016 film ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]''.{{WebCite|url=https://gizmodo.com/star-wars-acolyte-influences-leslye-headland-1850342154|text=''The Acolyte''{{'s}} Leslye Headland Explains Her Show's Influences|author=Justin Carter|date=2023-04-16|work=[[Wikipedia:Gizmodo|''Gizmodo'']]|archivedate=20230416191920}} Amandla Stenberg wrote about the motivations and inner lives of Osha and Mae, with separate binders for each twin to inform her approach as a performer and differentiating the characters.{{WebCite|url=https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/culture/video/amandla-stenberg-talks-star-wars-acolyte-110852564|text=Amandla Stenberg talks 'Star Wars: The Acolyte'|date=2024-06-05|work=[[Wikipedia:Good Morning America|''Good Morning America'']]|archivedate=20240605154229}} Indara was inspired by the character [[Wikipedia:Trinity (The Matrix)|Trinity]] from [[Wikipedia:The Wachowskis|the Wachowskis']] [[Wikipedia:The Matrix (franchise)|''The Matrix'']] film franchise (1999—2021), played by [[Carrie-Anne Moss]], who Headland also cast as Master Indara.{{WebCite|url=https://www.empireonline.com/tv/news/acolyte-carrie-anne-moss-jedi-master-indara-inspired-by-trinity-exclusive|text=The Acolyte: Carrie-Anne Moss' Jedi Master Indara Is 'Very Much Inspired By Trinity' – Exclusive|author=Ben Travis|work=[[Wikipedia:Empire (magazine)|''Empire'']]|archivedate=20240405140812}} For the first episode, "Lost / Found," Headland described the character's demeanor as both relaxed and controlled; a mix of Lucas' Skywalker saga Jedi character [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and the character O-Ren Ishii from ''Kill Bill''.{{SW|url=lost-found-trivia-gallery-the-acolyte|text="Lost / Found" Trivia Gallery | The Acolyte}} {{C|Slide 7}} Mae's accomplice, [[The Stranger|Qimir]], is played by [[Manny Jacinto]] as a scoundrel archetype based on [[Wikipedia:Johnny Depp|Johnny Depp]]'s performance of [[Wikipedia:Jack Sparrow|Jack Sparrow]] in the [[Wikipedia:Pirates of the Caribbean (film series)|''Pirates of the Caribbean'']] film series (2003–2017). Jacinto also compared Qimir's movements to the [[Wikipedia:Silent film|silent film]] works by [[Wikipedia:Buster Keaton|Buster Keaton]] and [[Wikipedia:Charlie Chaplin|Charlie Chaplin]] in the early 20th century.{{WebCite|url=https://www.digitalspy.com/tv/ustv/a61005293/the-acolyte-manny-jacinto|text=The Acolyte's Manny Jacinto reveals the surprising influence on his new Star Wars character|author=Ali Griffiths|date=2024-06-05|work=[[Wikipedia:Digital Spy|''Digital Spy'']]|archivedate=20240605193926}} Jacinto appreciated the duality of his character as a dream role for an actor, being able to emphasize the comic qualities of Qimir and then the stillness of the Stranger.{{SWYouTube|JzJmJ07GCng|The Acolyte | Manny Jacinto on Duality | Disney+}} The fourth and fifth episodes, respectively titled "[[Day (episode)|Day]]" and "[[Night]]," were partly inspired by two [[Wikipedia:Cinema of the United States|Hollywood]] science fiction films: [[Wikipedia:Ridley Scott|Ridley Scott's]] [[1979]] [[Wikipedia:Alien (film)|''Alien'']] and [[Wikipedia:John McTiernan|John McTiernan's]] [[1987]] [[Wikipedia:Predator (film)|''Predator'']].{{SW|url=night-trivia-gallery-the-acolyte|text="Night" Trivia Gallery | The Acolyte}} {{C|Slide 3}} Given his dual role as the Stranger, Jacinto was additionally inspired by [[Wikipedia:Toshiro Mifune|Toshiro Mifune's]] performance as the warrior Kikushiyo in 1954's [[Wikipedia:Seven Samurai|''Seven Samurai'']], a Kurosawa film named 七人の侍 in Japanese, and [[Wikipedia:Jackie Chan|Jackie Chan's]] performance as the martial artist [[Wikipedia:Wong Fei-hung|Wong Fei-hung]] in the [[Wikipedia:Cinema of Hong Kong|Hong Kong]] film [[Wikipedia:Drunken Master|''Drunken Master'']], released as 醉拳 in [[1978]].{{SW|url=news/the-acolyte-the-stranger-revealed|text=The Acolyte's Manny Jacinto Unmasked}} ====Production design==== {{Quote|If you look at periods of extended peace in history, you have things like the Renaissance, where art, design, architecture, and clothing are allowed to flourish because the money, resources, and creativity are available to make beautiful things. So, that was part of the design ethos that Kevin took onboard, as well as the costume design. The costumes, the lightsabers, even to some extent the ships, feel less brutal and more designed and finessed. The Jedi's robes have more gold and are more regal. There are more curves and flowing lines in the ships.|Visual effects supervisor Julian Foddy|{{SW|url=news/ilm-the-acolyte-vfx-interview|text=Lightsabers & Magic: Visual Effects Supervisor Julian Foddy on The Acolyte's Creatures and Weapons of the Jedi}}}} Brendok's mountain retreat was inspired by the 1947 British film [[Wikipedia:Black Narcissus|''Black Narcissus'']] by [[Wikipedia:Powell and Pressburger|Michael Powell and Emeric Pressburger]]—set at a nuns' mountain retreat in the [[Wikipedia:British Raj|Indian]] [[Wikipedia:Himalayas|Himalayas]]—coupled with the [[Wikipedia:Hoover Dam|Hoover Dam]] in the United States. For Coruscant and its Jedi Temple, production designer [[Kevin Jenkins]] and visual effects supervisor [[Julian Foddy]] decided aligning moreso with the prequel trilogy's establishing shots than the ground-level perspective shown in the 2022 television series ''[[Star Wars: Andor]]'', but with distinctive aesthetics echoing the 1971 [[Wikipedia:William Friedkin|William Friedkin]] film [[Wikipedia:The French Connection (film)|''The French Connection'']] and 1970s [[Wikipedia:New York City|New York City]]: in particular, a desaturated and photorealistic "retro" atmosphere of haziness. Jenkins heeded George Lucas' 1977 film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope''{{'s}}]] lived-in aesthetic, stating that the core of ''Star Wars'' is [[Wikipedia:Stanley Kubrick|Stanley Kubrick's]] 1968 film [[Wikipedia:2001: A Space Odyssey|''2001: A Space Odyssey'']] "with dirt"—he learned from the designs of ''A New Hope'' production crew [[John Barry]], [[Norman Reynolds]], and Ralph McQuarrie while cinematographer Chris Teague used anamorphic lenses for ''The Acolyte'', with film grain being added to the footage. Jenkins also likened Headland's episodic structure to the cliffhanger-based approach of the [[Wikipedia:Flash Gordon|''Flash Gordon'']] serials, and further compared the High Republic Era to the height of the [[Wikipedia:Roman Empire|Roman Empire]], incorporating vivid colors in ''The Acolyte''{{'s}} production design while maintaining a uniformity of Jedi designs previously shown in ''The High Republic'' publishing initiative. Jenkins said Olega's city was "essentially [[Wikipedia:Casablanca|Casablanca]] in space" with its blue and red color palette,{{Lucasfilm|url=news/lucasfilm-on-location-the-acolyte|text=Lucasfilm on Location: ''The Acolyte''}} while StarWars.com stated it was inspired by [[Wikipedia:Marrakesh|Marrakesh]], another city in [[Wikipedia:Morocco|Morocco]].{{SW|url=revenge-justice-trivia-gallery-the-acolyte|text="Revenge / Justice" Trivia Gallery | The Acolyte}} {{C|Slide 1}} Costume designer [[Jennifer Bryan]] researched [[Trisha Biggar]]'s prequel trilogy costumes at the [[Lucasfilm Archives]] at [[Skywalker Ranch]], which particularly informed the clothing of the High Republic Era Jedi along with existing designs, such as High Republic Jedi symbols, from the multimedia project. The color palette of Osha's civilian clothing was informed by the era of the [[Wikipedia:Vietnam War|Vietnam War]] that preceded George Lucas' original trilogy and the ''Star Wars'' design principle of greeblies and badges. Another distinctive ''Star Wars'' fashion staple, the poncho, was also incorporated in civilian clothing featured in later episodes. Bryan further took inspiration from warrior cultures from [[Wikipedia:Anatolia|Asia Minor]], [[Wikipedia:East Africa|East Africa]], [[Wikipedia:North Africa|North Africa]], and the Roman and [[Wikipedia:Byzantine Empire|Byzantine Empires]]: "It needs to look like it's put together from these different historical eras of warriors, but not specific to any one culture." Mae's assassin attire in particular was informed by samurai elements. Bryan also thought that Jodie Turner-Smith's elegance complemented the design made for Mother Aniseya, while [[Yord Fandar]]'s fastidiousness and "lustrous drape" called for fabrics slightly different from those used on other Jedi costumes, with his more appearance-conscious attitude reflected in a cloak informed by Roman senators' [[Wikipedia:Toga|togas]].{{SW|url=news/dressing-the-acolyte-costumes-feature|text=Dressing ''The Acolyte'': The Stranger and an Assassin Hunt the Jedi of the High Republic — Updated}} The production gave special thanks to the historic Lucasfilm Archives at Skywalker Ranch and George Lucas' new [[Wikipedia:Lucas Museum of Narrative Art|Lucas Museum of Narrative Art]]. Leslye Headland emphasized using practical techniques in her direction of the production design, cinematography, and visual effects. ====Filming in Madeira, Wales, and England==== {{Quote|What was really interesting about Wales, especially Southern Wales, is that it had a very raw sort of feeling to it. What also gravitated us to the area was the location of the landing of the [Jedi starship] ''Polan'', which became our anchor base. Just behind us in that same valley was this old 18th century dam, this massive black stone brick wall. And nearby was this wonderful forest where the whole floor was a bed of moss growing up the trees that I thought could be where the girls are first introduced. So with the moss forest, the valley vistas and this dam that's singing out to be used, Wales just seemed to tick all the boxes.|Kevin Jenkins|}} Filming began in Europe's autumn in 2022 and lasted until May of 2023.{{Lucasfilm|url=news/julian-foddy-acolyte|text=''The Acolyte'' Visual Effects Supervisor Julian Foddy}} Filming was largely done on location on [[Wikipedia:Portugal|Portugal's]] [[Wikipedia:Madeira|Madeira]] archipelago off the coast of [[Wikipedia:Africa|Africa]] and in and around the mountainous forest of the [[Wikipedia:Brecon Beacons National Park|Bannau Brycheiniog National Park]] (Brecon Beacons) in [[Wikipedia:Wales|Wales]]. Interior scenes were shot at [[Shinfield Studios]] in [[Wikipedia:Berkshire|Berkshire]], [[Wikipedia:England|England]]. Shooting also took place at the woods of Berkshire's [[Wikipedia:Englefield House|Englefield Estate]].{{WebCite|url=https://www.timeout.com/news/where-was-the-acolyte-filmed-the-surprising-locations-behind-the-new-star-wars-series-060524|text=Where was 'The Acolyte' filmed? The surprising locations behind the new Star Wars series|author=Gregory James Wakeman|date=2024-06-05|work=[[Wikipedia:Time Out (magazine)|''Time Out'']]|archivedate=20240609171023}} Manny Jacinto prepared for his role as Qimir in the relative seclusion of the nearby town of [[Wikipedia:Windsor, Berkshire|Windsor]]. [[Sur Film]] provided production services in Portugal. The crew initially used Madeira for the planet [[Khofar]]'s jungles, but they made use of other parts of the archipelago for scenes set on [[Olega]], [[Ueda]], and [[Bal'demnic]]{{EmailCite|email=File:AtlasEmail-2025-10-24.png|creator=[[Jason Fry]]|date=2025-10-24}} as well. Khofar's forest perimeter was shot at Pico do Arieiro and digitally inserted to shots of the Fanal Forest and Poço das Casas. The interior of the jungles was filmed at Shinfield Studios, with practical "mega trees" occupying the soundstage and even some of its stage doors. A short scene of Ueda was shot at Ponta de São Lourenço for its "brown, dusty Western" aesthetic, and the establishing shot of Olega was shot at Pedra D'Eira. Olega's city scenes were shot in Shinfield Studios. The exterior island shots of Bal'demnic were captured along the northern coastline of western Madeira, and the mouth of Stranger's cave is located at Ribeira de Janela. "Fifteen minutes down the road," the crew found the Porto Moniz Rockpools and shot the Stranger's bathing scene there. [[File:BuntaCadlan.jpg|thumb|right|300px|A dead oak tree in southern Wales is dressed in yellow willow-like branches.]] An empty lot and several fields near the [[Wikipedia:Trago Mills|Trago Mills]] department store in [[Wikipedia:Merthyr Tydfil|Merthyr Tydfil]] were used for ''The Acolyte''{{'s}} production in Wales.{{WebCite|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cx92exjz98ro|text=Star Wars: The Acolyte brings Wales to the galaxy far, far away|author=Ryan Leston|work=[[Wikipedia:BBC|BBC News]]|archivedate=20240714094721}} The series introduces the planet Brendok, with all of its exterior scenes being shot in Southern Wales—aside from the campfire scene, shot at England's [[Pinewood Studios]] in [[Wikipedia:Iver|Iver Heath]], [[Wikipedia:Buckinghamshire|Buckinghamshire]]. The crew filmed in the mossy Taf Fechan forest, a dead oak tree in the Cadlan Woods that was decorated for the yellow willow-like [[bunta tree]], and the drained Upper Neuadd Reservoir of Bannau Brycheiniog. The Upper Neuadd Dam served as the exterior of the Brendok [[Brendok coven|witch coven]]'s [[Brendok fortress|mountain retreat]]. The dam informed the design of the retreat, and its interior scenes were shot at Shinfield Studios. The series was shot with cameras and [[Wikipedia:Arri|ARRI]] ALFA lenses supplied by ARRI Rental. ====Post-production in London, Canada, India, Austria, Australia, and California==== {{Quote|The musical themes in ''The Acolyte'' are tied more to an emotion or a point of view or a literary theme than they are to a particular character.|Composer [[Michael Abels]]|{{SW|url=news/the-acolyte-music-michael-abels-interview|text=Scoring ''The Acolyte'': Composing for the Jedi, the Witches, and the Many Moods of the Stranger}}}} The series was edited by [[Miikka Leskinen]] and [[Cheryl Potter]] with [[Wikipedia:Avid Technology|Avid]] editing equipment supplied by HireWorks. Sound services were provided by [[Skywalker Sound]] in [[Wikipedia:Marin County, California|Marin County, California]], with [[Brian Chumney]] as the supervising sound editor. Visual effects post-production was led by [[Industrial Light & Magic]] (ILM), a Lucasfilm subsidiary, with its studios in [[Wikipedia:London|London]], England, and [[Wikipedia:Vancouver|Vancouver]], [[Wikipedia:Canada|Canada]], extending through to the late end of winter in 2024. ILM's new office in [[Wikipedia:Mumbai|Mumbai]], [[Wikipedia:India|India]], also contributed to the nearly 3000 shots made for ''The Acolyte'', marking one of its first completed works. Additional visual effects were made by [[Yannix]] and [[SDFX Studios]], as well as the London-based [[Outpost Visual Effects]] and the Vancouver-based [[beloFX]]. Visual effects were also partly produced in [[Wikipedia:Melbourne|Melbourne]], [[Wikipedia:Australia|Australia]], with [[Rising Sun Pictures]] of nearby [[Wikipedia:Adelaide|Adelaide]] and the [[Wikipedia:Los Angeles|Los Angeles]]–based [[Luma Pictures]] having contributed too, as did [[Hybride]] of [[Ubisoft]] in [[Wikipedia:Montreal|Montreal]], Canada. [[Proof Inc.]] additionally provided visualization services. Unlike previous productions centered at ILM's headquarters in [[Wikipedia:San Francisco|San Francisco]], California, ILM London served as the visual effects post-production hub for ''The Acolyte'', led by production supervisor Julian Foddy. The visual effects crew worked closely with the creatures' department led by [[Neal Scanlan]] and editors Leskinen and Potter for the hybrid practical effects and computer graphics shots of the [[umbramoth]]s. The score of ''The Acolyte'' was composed by Michael Abels with additional music by [[Miguel Bezanilla]], [[Cameron Moody]], and [[Robert Wallace]]. The score was recorded at [[Wikipedia:Synchron Stage Vienna|Synchron Stage Vienna]] in [[Wikipedia:Austria|Austria]] under the conductor [[Gottfried Rabl]]. Abels pointed out that the musical themes were emotion-based rather than character-based, taking the example of the "duality of the characters" Mae and Osha when they are vengeful or hopeful, with the same musical motifs occurring with different characters. Abels added that "You can tell I've had a lot of fun playing with how the Force is used and who uses it and what we think about whether that use of the Force is good or bad." While the score does not foreshadow or connect the music associated with Qimir with the Stranger, when the Stranger is revealed at the end of "Day," the music includes a nod to [[Ben Solo's theme|Kylo Ren's theme]]. In keeping with the cinematic echo with ''Rashomon'', the two flashback episodes include scenes in which the visuals are the same yet the music is different to accentuate different emotional perspectives. ====Production finance==== {{Quote|''The Acolyte'' had many strong reviews and did well in the ratings its first week out, but you ultimately opted against a second season. Why didn't you move forward? And can you offer any hint as to how ''Skeleton Crew'' is doing, or its future?''"
"''So as it relates to ''Acolyte'', we were happy with our performance, but it wasn't where we needed it to be given the cost structure of that title, quite frankly, to go and make a season two. As you said, the reviews have been excellent on ''Skeleton Crew'', so we'll have to see how that all plays out as it moves forward.|Interviewer Josef Adalian for ''Vulture'' and Alan Bergman, co-chair of Disney Entertainment|{{WebCite|url=https://www.vulture.com/article/how-disney-finally-made-streaming-profitable.html|text=How Disney (Finally) Made Streaming Profitable|author=Josef Adalian|date=2024-12-19|work=[[Wikipedia:Vulture (website)|''Vulture'']]|archivedate=20241220183136}}}} ''The Acolyte'' was produced with the support of the British Film Commission and the UK Government's High-End Television Tax Relief, the Canadian Film or Video Production Services Tax Credit, the [[Wikipedia:British Columbia|Province of British Columbia]] Production Service Tax Credit, [[Wikipedia:Quebec|Québec's]] Production Services Tax Credit, Portugal's Tourism and Cinema Fund, and the Australian Government's PDV Offset tax rebate. Visual effects production in Australia was also supported by [[Wikipedia:VicScreen|VicScreen]] in [[Wikipedia:Victoria (state)|Victoria]] and in [[Wikipedia:South Australia|South Australia]] with the support of the [[Wikipedia:South Australian Film Corporation|South Australian Film Corporation]]. While media outlets reported that the series' production cost was around $180 million in [[Wikipedia:United States dollar|US dollars]], Lucasfilm had registered a subsidiary high-end television program production company in [[Wikipedia:England and Wales|England and Wales]] named Blue Stockings (UK). The company's publicly filed audit covering [[March 24]], 2021 to [[September 24]] 2023, reports that "the cost was forecasted to be over the production budget" but are approved and fully funded by Lucasfilm as of September 24, 2024, with the production having been certified by the [[Wikipedia:British Film Institute|British Film Institute]] in the interim as "British,"{{WebCite|url=https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/13289804/filing-history|text=BLUE STOCKINGS (UK) LIMITED filing history|work=[[Wikipedia:Companies House|Companies House]]|archivedate=20240928160744}} which would qualify the production for [[Wikipedia:HM Revenue and Customs|HM Revenue and Customs]] [[Wikipedia:Tax credit|tax credits]]{{WebCite|url=https://britishfilmcommission.org.uk/plan-your-production/accessing-uk-tax-reliefs|text=Accessing UK Tax Reliefs|work=British Film Commission|archivedate=20240523113309}} for the ultimate parent company, The Walt Disney Company. The report further indicates that UK television production expenditure between those dates totalled £172,320,864 in [[Wikipedia:Pound sterling|British pound sterling]], equivalent to around $230 million US dollars. Based on the UK tax relief scheme, the same filing claims a total of £34,839,012 pounds of expenditure credits for the relevant periods—which would bring Blue Stockings' production cost down to £137,481,852 pounds, equivalent to just under $184 million US dollars.
